    StartersFig prosciutto, olive and cheddar picksProsciutto wrapped figs, warm orange olives and cheddar shards on toothpicksHow to make it6 figs, halved100g prosciutto200g olives1 orange, peel in strips1 tsp fennel seeds150g vintage cheddarWrap each fig half in a piece of prosciutto.Warm the olives in a small pan with the orange peel and fennel seeds until fragrant.Break the cheddar into shards and push everything onto toothpicks so nobody gets greasy fingers on the cards.Vesper's train dinner saladShaved fennel, orange segments and toasted hazelnuts on butter lettuce, Dijon dressingHow to make it60g hazelnuts1 fennel bulb2 oranges1 butter lettuce2 tsp Dijon mustard1 tbsp white wine vinegar3 tbsp extra virgin olive oilsalt and pepper, to tasteToast the hazelnuts at 170°C for 8 minutes, cool and roughly chop.Shave the fennel paper thin and cut the oranges into segments.Whisk the mustard, vinegar and oil into a dressing and season with salt and pepper. Toss the lettuce, fennel, orange and nuts together with the dressing at the last second.Nassau prawn and crab frittersBond's stop in the BahamasHow to make itAs written, serves 4Crisp golden fritters of chopped prawn and crab with capsicum, celery, spring onion and scotch bonnet, with a zingy lime and chilli aioli.Chop 250g peeled green prawns and mix with 150g crab meat, half a finely diced red capsicum, a celery stick, 2 spring onions and a little chopped scotch bonnet.Whisk in 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 egg and 125ml milk to a thick batter.Fry spoonfuls at 180°C for 3 minutes until golden.Mix 150g mayo with lime zest and juice, a crushed garlic clove and chilli sauce.Grilled octopus with lemon and oreganoFuel for the poker game. Buy in, ten million.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsBalkan grilled lambGarlic rosemary lamb chops grilled hot, roasted red peppers, garlic yoghurtHow to make it1.2kg lamb shoulder chops5 garlic cloves2 sprigs of rosemary1 lemon4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil3 red capsicums200g Greek yoghurtsalt, to tasteCrush 4 of the garlic cloves and mix with the chopped rosemary, lemon juice and zest and the oil. Rub over the lamb.Cover and marinate in the fridge overnight.Roast the capsicums at 220°C until blistered, then peel and slice.Grill the lamb hot until charred outside and pink inside.Crush the last garlic clove into the yoghurt with a pinch of salt. Serve with the lamb and capsicums.Venice seafood risotto with gremolataThe sinking house in VeniceHow to make itAs written, serves 4Carnaroli cooked slowly in fish stock with white wine, loaded with prawns, mussels and squid, finished with butter and a sharp lemon, garlic and parsley gremolata.Soften 2 chopped shallots and 2 garlic cloves in 2 tbsp olive oil, add 350g carnaroli and toast 1 minute.Add 125ml white wine, then 1.2L hot fish stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 16 minutes.Add 300g peeled green prawns, 500g mussels and 200g sliced squid, cover and cook 3 minutes until the mussels open.Stir in 30g butter.Chop parsley, lemon zest and a garlic clove for gremolata and scatter over.SweetsChocolate fondantWarm chocolate cakes, molten centre. Melt the chocolate and butter together and let it cool a little.Whisk the eggs, yolks and sugar until pale, then combine with the chocolate and fold in the flour.Divide between the moulds and bake at 220°C for 9 minutes.Turn out straight away so the centres run.DrinksThe Vesper gin and vodka martiniShaken with white vermouth.
